## Example 2.5 {#dc2-example-2-5 .dc-lesson}

<p>Differentiate the following expressions with respect to <span data-math="x"></span>.</p><div class="dc-problem-list"><div><span class="part">a)</span><span data-math="y=\ln(3x-2)"></span></div><div><span class="part">b)</span><span data-math="y=\ln(x^2+1)"></span></div><div><span class="part">c)</span><span data-math="y=\ln(1+e^x)"></span></div></div><p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 12 · Example 2.5</p>

::: notes
(a) y'=3/(3x-2), original domain x>2/3. (b) y'=2x/(x^2+1), all real x. (c) y'=e^x/(1+e^x), all real x. The numerator is the derivative of the entire argument; the denominator keeps the entire argument. In (b), the function is defined even for negative x because x^2+1>0. For (c), keep the sum intact; ln(1+e^x) is not ln1+ln(e^x). Work in OneNote; around five minutes.
:::
